title: How Much of the Standing Arrears Is Collected When Ridgecrest Advantage Coverage Is Restored
content:
The share of the arrears standing when the coverage ended that the plan collects on the restoration of a Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan enrollment follows the plan premium payments standing on the premium account and how long ago the coverage ended.

1. Where at least 2 plan premium payments stand on the premium account and the coverage ended less than 2 whole months before the handling date, the share of the arrears the plan collects on restoration is half of them, that is 50 per cent, the rest being billed over the coverage months that follow.
2. Where at least 2 plan premium payments stand on the premium account and the coverage ended at least 2 whole months before the handling date, that share is three quarters of them, that is 75 per cent.
3. Where fewer than 2 plan premium payments stand on the premium account, that share is the whole of them, that is 100 per cent.

The third entry is reached on the payments standing on the account alone: with 0 or 1 plan premium payment there, how long ago the coverage ended makes no difference and the whole of the arrears is collected.

*Hypothetical case: arrears standing when the coverage ended of 240.00 USD.* With 3 plan premium payments on the account and a coverage end date 1 whole month before the handling date, the plan collects half of them, 120.00 USD. With the same 3 payments and a coverage end date 4 whole months before the handling date, it collects three quarters of them, 180.00 USD. With a single plan premium payment on the account, it collects the whole of them, 240.00 USD.
